default.summary: llm-d-router's built-in config, used when a run names none: queue depth, KV cache and prefix scorers, then the highest score.
default.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: queue-scorer
- type: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
- type: prefix-cache-scorer
- type: metrics-data-source
- type: core-metrics-extractor
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
    weight: 2
  - pluginRef: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
    weight: 2
  - pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer
    weight: 3

load-aware.summary: Sends each request to the least-loaded instance.
load-aware.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: load-aware-scorer
- type: max-score-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: load-aware-scorer
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker

prefix-affinity.summary: Keeps requests that share a prefix on the instance that served it first.
prefix-affinity.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: approx-prefix-cache-producer
- type: prefix-cache-scorer
- type: max-score-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker

queue.summary: Sends each request to the instance with the shortest queue.
queue.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: queue-scorer
- type: max-score-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker

queue-kv.summary: Weighs queue depth and free KV cache equally.
queue-kv.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: queue-scorer
- type: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
- type: max-score-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: queue-scorer
    weight: 2.0
  - pluginRef: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
    weight: 2.0
  - pluginRef: max-score-picker

random.summary: Spreads requests at random; the baseline every scorer has to beat.
random.yaml:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
plugins:
- type: random-picker
- type: single-profile-handler
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: random-picker

setup.script:
# the stack that priced this report (needs git and Go)
git clone --branch v0.15.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim.git inference-sim
test "$(git -C inference-sim rev-parse HEAD)" = 762f1605ff27cd825d6b2cb2d9e991cd4b864c91 || echo "inference-sim: v0.15.0 moved off 762f1605" >&2
(cd inference-sim && go build -o blis main.go)
export PATH="$PWD/inference-sim:$PATH"

git clone --branch 0.5.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-catalog.git blis-catalog
test "$(git -C blis-catalog rev-parse HEAD)" = b5550f750cb51571498577fbdc1c68f78cda67db || echo "blis-catalog: 0.5.0 moved off b5550f75" >&2
export BLIS_CATALOG="$PWD/blis-catalog"

git clone --branch v0.3.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-registry.git blis-registry
test "$(git -C blis-registry rev-parse HEAD)" = 96bead697172ab7f2cf8346e04e65b837014d867 || echo "blis-registry: v0.3.0 moved off 96bead69" >&2
export BLIS_REGISTRY="$PWD/blis-registry"

# the commands run from this repo: router configs live here, scenarios/ is where you save each scenario
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-config-search.git && cd blis-config-search && mkdir -p scenarios
setup.sweep:
# in the blis-config-search checkout, after the install script
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install pyyaml
python3 -I scripts/run_experiment.py reports/glm53flash-h100-chatbot-kernel-0001/spec.yaml --dry-run --catalog "$BLIS_CATALOG"
python3 -I scripts/run_experiment.py reports/glm53flash-h100-chatbot-kernel-0001/spec.yaml \
  --blis "$(command -v blis)" --catalog "$BLIS_CATALOG" --registry "$BLIS_REGISTRY" \
  --out repro/

spec_yaml:
name: glm53flash-h100-chatbot-kernel-0001
scenario:
  model: glm-5.3-flash
  hardware: h100
  workload: chatbot
  gpus: 16
  slo:
    itl_p99: 20ms
  engine:
    quantization: fp8
    cache_dtype: fp8
  concurrency:
  - 2
  - 8
  - 16
  - 64
  - 256
sweeps:
- name: shape-and-ep
  narrative: EP should pay most at tp 8 and fade as dp grows, since wider dp already
    splits the batch and EP adds dispatch on top.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 4
    - 8
    - 16
    dp:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 4
    - 8
    - 16
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - false
    - true
- name: batch-caps-vs-shape
  narrative: The sequence cap should bind well before the token cap on short chatbot
    prompts, and hardest on one wide instance.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 16
    - 8
    - 2
    - 1
    dp:
    - 1
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    max_num_seqs:
    - 16
    - 32
    - 64
    - 256
    - 1024
    max_num_batched_tokens:
    - 2048
    - 8192
    - 32768
- name: moe-dispatch
  narrative: DeepEP backends should lose to allgather/pplx at small dp and close the
    gap as dp widens, where the token cap admits them.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 4
    - 8
    dp:
    - 2
    - 4
    - 8
    - 16
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    all2all_backend:
    - allgather_reducescatter
    - deepep_high_throughput
    - deepep_low_latency
    - deepep_v2
    - pplx
    max_num_batched_tokens:
    - 2048
    - 8192
- name: eplb-vs-dispatch
  narrative: Redundant experts should help most at the widest dp, where an uneven
    expert load stalls the most ranks.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 4
    dp:
    - 2
    - 4
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    all2all_backend:
    - allgather_reducescatter
    - deepep_high_throughput
    eplb:
      enable_eplb:
      - true
      num_redundant_experts:
      - 0
      - 32
      - 64
- name: graph-capture
  narrative: Full graph capture should beat PIECEWISE by a few percent at every shape,
    and NONE should roughly halve throughput.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 16
    - 8
    - 2
    - 1
    dp:
    - 1
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    cudagraph_mode:
    - NONE
    - PIECEWISE
    - FULL
    - FULL_DECODE_ONLY
    - FULL_AND_PIECEWISE
- name: capture-size-vs-batch
  narrative: A small capture size should cost throughput only when max_num_seqs lets
    the batch grow past it.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 8
    - 2
    dp:
    - 1
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    cudagraph_mode:
    - PIECEWISE
    - FULL
    max_cudagraph_capture_size:
    - 64
    - 256
    - 512
    max_num_seqs:
    - 64
    - 512
- name: prefill-admission
  narrative: Chunking prefills below the 256-token median prompt should cut the ITL
    tail but cost throughput, most on one wide instance.
  num-instances:
  - 1
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 16
    - 8
    - 2
    - 1
    dp:
    - 1
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    long_prefill_token_threshold:
    - 256
    - 1024
    - 4096
    max_num_batched_tokens:
    - 2048
    - 8192
- name: routing
  narrative: With only two endpoints, routing should move throughput a few percent
    at most, slightly more when the batch cap binds.
  num-instances:
  - 2
  parallel:
    tp:
    - 1
    - 4
    - 8
    dp:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 8
    enable_expert_parallel:
    - true
  engine:
    max_num_seqs:
    - 64
    - 1024
  router:
    endpoint_picker_config:
    - random.yaml
    - queue.yaml
    - load-aware.yaml
    - queue-kv.yaml
    - prefix-affinity.yaml
